name: Panama
summary_text: Panama is workable for trans visitors. Same-sex activity was decriminalised in 2008 by presidential decree on constitutional nondiscrimination grounds. Legal gender recognition exists but requires surgery — a resident-facing barrier. There is no anti-discrimination law covering gender identity, and in March 2023 the Supreme Court ruled same-sex marriage is not a constitutional right, signaling judicial conservatism. Panama City has a visible, established trans community and hosts regional LGBT organising. No traveler-facing restrictions exist: no bathroom laws, no border friction, no documented police targeting pattern. Social hostility is moderate — machista culture persists, and trans women face documented employment exclusion — but violent targeting is far below Northern Triangle levels.

sources.title: Panama | Outright International
sources.claim_summary: Outright International country overview (updated March 2026): same-sex activity legal since 2008 (Presidential Decree 332); but same-sex marriage ruled not a constitutional human right by the Supreme Court (March 2023); no explicit SOGISC discrimination protections (amendment blocked by the National Assembly in 2024); harassment, violence and discrimination not formally recognised as hate crimes; conservative religious actors consistently oppose advances.

Equaldex data for Panama: homosexuality legal, marriage banned, gender change legal but requires surgery, no nonbinary recognition, no hate-crime protections, no employment/housing discrimination protections, blood donation banned (indefinite deferral), conversion therapy not banned. Only 12% approve of same-sex marriage (AmericasBarometer 2023, ranked #18 of 22).

sources.title: Panama Supreme Court judge withdraws draft ruling against marriage
sources.claim_summary: Washington Blade (Feb 2018): a Panama Supreme Court judge withdrew a draft ruling against same-sex marriage after public outcry - part of the court's long-running marriage litigation.

sources.title: Guna Yala: The islands where women make the rules
sources.claim_summary: BBC Travel (Aug 2018): 'Guna Yala: The islands where women make the rules' - in the indigenous Guna territory off Panama, a flourishing 'third gender' community (omeggid) is celebrated, with natural gender equality and tolerance of gender fluidity - a striking cultural counterpoint to national law.

sources.title: Panama | Outright International
sources.claim_summary: Outright International country overview for Panama (updated March 2026): same-sex conduct legal since 2008 (Presidential Decree 332); legal gender recognition possible; but no marriage or adoption, and the March 2023 Supreme Court ruling that same-sex marriage is not a constitutional human right foreclosed domestic avenues; no SOGI anti-discrimination laws (amendments blocked in 2024); police abuse of trans women reported.

sources.title: Report: Panama Supreme Court judge rules against same-sex marriage
sources.claim_summary: Washington Blade (Oct 2017): a Panama Supreme Court judge ruled against same-sex marriage in a draft opinion - the first of the court's rulings in the marriage cases.
